The patient presents with significant hyponatremia (Na 122 mEq/L), low serum osmolality (265 mOsm/kg), and inappropriately high urine sodium (45 mEq/L) and osmolality (334 mOsm/kg), which is the classic diagnostic profile for Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuretic Hormone (SIADH). With normal thyroid function, normal adrenal function (implied by context/exclusion of other causes), and negative imaging for lung cancer or CNS masses, this is likely idiopathic or drug-induced SIADH causing the mental status changes.
